article:
We recently completed a full interior repaint on a 3,200-square-foot home in South Loveland that the homeowners had just purchased a week prior. This was a whole-home project covering all walls and ceilings—the kind of work that sets the tone for how a family will experience their new space. In Northern Colorado, where dry air and intense sunlight can fade paint faster than most regions, choosing the right contractor and products matters more than people realize.

What We Did

Our team masked off every surface that wasn’t getting painted—floors, trim, doors, baseboards, windows, and built-ins. We didn’t cut corners on prep. We shot all the walls with Sherwin-Williams Natural Linen in a satin Super Paint finish, which is a durable, washable finish built to last. The ceilings got a flat bright white coat applied separately to ensure clean lines and even coverage. Because the house is 3,200 square feet and the basement was added to the scope mid-project, our crew worked methodically to knock out the application while maintaining the attention to detail that separates professional work from the discount kind.

We set up airflow throughout the home to help the paint cure properly. That’s not a luxury; it’s a necessity in a space where your family lives and breathes every day.

Why Prep Matters More Than Paint

Here’s what we’ve learned doing interior painting across Northern Colorado: the paint itself is only half the job. Every cheap contractor cuts corners on prep, and that’s where you pay the price later—with peeling, uneven coverage, and a finish that doesn’t last. We protect everything that shouldn’t be painted. We seal off your most valuable asset—your home—like we mean it. That means careful masking, controlled airflow, and respect for the spaces where your family actually lives.

The Result

This South Loveland homeowner now has a freshly painted interior with Sherwin-Williams products that are built to withstand daily use. The satin finish on the walls is durable and washable—practical for a lived-in home. The flat white on the ceilings stays clean without that plastic sheen. Both finishes will hold up for years in our climate. This is the kind of work that doesn’t just look good on move-in day; it protects your investment and gives you a home that feels new.

If you’re thinking about interior painting in Northern Colorado, call us for a quote. We’re licensed, insured with $1M liability, approved by Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore, and we know our crews.

faqs.q: What does a whole home interior repaint include?
faqs.a: We paint all walls and ceilings throughout your home using premium products like Sherwin-Williams Natural Linen in satin finish for walls and flat bright white for ceilings. Every surface that shouldn’t be painted—trim, doors, baseboards, built-ins, windows—gets fully masked and protected. For a 3,200 square foot home, we typically complete the project in 2–3 days with a full prep day and dedicated crews who know what they’re doing.

faqs.q: How much does interior painting cost in Northern Colorado?
faqs.a: Interior painting in Northern Colorado typically ranges from $2,500 to $8,000+ depending on square footage, ceiling height, prep work needed, and product selection. A 3,200 square foot whole home repaint falls in the $5,000–$7,000 range with premium Sherwin-Williams paint and professional prep. We’re licensed and insured with $1M liability, so you’re getting quality that lasts.

faqs.q: What makes Keystone Painting different from other interior painting contractors?
faqs.a: We’re Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore approved, licensed and insured with $1M liability coverage, and we actually know our crews—no revolving door of subcontractors. We treat your home like it’s our own: detail-oriented masking, premium products, and crews we trust to deliver quality at every turn.

faqs.q: How do you protect my floors, trim, and furniture during interior painting?
faqs.a: We fully mask all floors, baseboards, trim, doors, windows, and built-ins before we spray or brush anything. Our crew establishes airflow and works methodically to ensure paint only goes where it should. No overspray, no damage to your home—that’s the standard we hold ourselves to on every project.
